Question: A man walks \(x\) miles due west, turns \(150^\circ\) to his left and walks \(3\) miles in the new direction. If he finishes at a point \(\sqrt3\) miles from his starting point, then \(x\) is

Choices.E:
not uniquely determined by the given
information

Solution:
Let \(O\) be the starting point, \(T\) the turning point, and \(P\) the finishing point. Since the first walk is due west, \(O\) is \(x\) miles east of \(T\). A \(150^\circ\) left turn from west points \(30^\circ\) south of east.

Let \(H\) be the perpendicular projection of \(P\) onto the east-west line through \(O\) and \(T\). In right triangle \(THP\), the hypotenuse \(TP\) is 3 and the angle at \(T\) is \(30^\circ\). The side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, so
\[
PH=\frac32.
\]
The Pythagorean theorem then gives
\[
TH=\sqrt{3^2-\left(\frac32\right)^2}
=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2},
\]
with \(H\) east of \(T\).

The given distance \(OP=\sqrt3\) supplies another right triangle, \(OHP\). Hence
\[
OH=\sqrt{(\sqrt3)^2-\left(\frac32\right)^2}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
The point \(O\) can lie either west or east of \(H\) by this distance. Because \(TH>OH\), both positions place \(O\) east of \(T\), as required. They give
\[
x=TH-OH=\sqrt3
\]
or
\[
x=TH+OH=2\sqrt3.
\]
These are the only two positions on the horizontal line at the required distance from \(H\), and both satisfy the original conditions. Thus \(x\) is not uniquely determined, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
